name: speed-quiet
title: Hooks and commands on a real archive, machine not busy
summary: How long an agent session waits for ctx. Hooks run on every session start, compaction and subagent start, so they are held to a 3-second limit and should take a small fraction of it.

metrics.label: Session start: rules and archive note
Read a turn with its neighbours

bar: every hook's slowest run under 1,000 ms
baseline: the 3-second limit Claude Code gives a hook, and the 1-second bar set here
meaning: With the machine quiet every hook takes 5 to 35 ms at the median. The compaction brief still failed the bar, at 1.2 s on its first run and about 35 ms after that. The same first-run figure appeared under heavy load, so it is not caused by load: the first brief after a while reads index pages that are no longer in memory. It is inside the 3-second limit, and it is the real cost after a compaction.
